title: incident blast-radius estimator and safe rollback planner
author: Anika Rao
release_notes:
- Adds an estimator to quantify potential blast radius for a given rollback or configuration change
- Provides a planner that emits a safe rollback checklist and staged cutoff points
- Exposes CLI commands sloctl estimate-blast and sloctl plan-rollback (no runtime behavior changes until planner accepted)
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight 'blast-radius estimator' and a complementary 'safe rollback planner' to slo-toolkit. The estimator simulates the expected impact (error budget burn,  p50/p95 latency shifts, request loss) for candidate rollbacks or configuration changes using recent SLO windows and historical traffic distributions. The planner generates a staged rollback/mitigation playbook (checklist with automated gating suggestions) and integrates with incident-bot to annotate runbooks with estimated impact and safe cutoff points.

Motivation: On many incidents engineers need a quick, quantitative sense of how far a rollback will affect customer-facing metrics before executing it. Previously teams relied on ad-hoc heuristics. This PR delivers an opinionated, reproducible estimator that is conservative by default and a planner that operationalizes staged rollbacks with explicit verification steps.

Design/Approach: The estimator uses a sampling-based simulator over recent SLO windows (configurable window size and weighting) and applies an "impact profile" derived from runtime signals (error_ratio, latency_shift, requests_per_minute). The planner consumes estimator output and optional runbook annotations to produce a multi-stage rollback plan with: (1) a soft cutoff (traffic split or feature flag step), (2) verification gates (synthetic checks + smoke assertions), (3) full revert instructions. All logic is config-driven and feature-flagged behind slo.featureEstimator.

CLI + API: Adds two commands to sloctl: "sloctl estimate-blast --config examples/incidents/estimator-profile.yaml --since 1h" and "sloctl plan-rollback --estimator-output /tmp/est.json --strategy conservative". The planner also exposes a JSON artifact that incident-bot can ingest to annotate a runbook comment with recommended actions and verification endpoints.

Checklist (PR readiness):
- [x] Estimator core algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Planner emits stable JSON schema and attachable runbook snippet
- [x] CLI plumbing and help text added
- [x] Documentation and example profiles included
- [x] E2E smoke test against a local SLO sandbox

Commits (high level):
- feat(estimator): sampling-based blast radius estimator and config parsing
- feat(planner): staged rollback planner and scheduler hooks for incident-bot annotation
- feat(cli): add sloctl estimate-blast and sloctl plan-rollback commands
- docs: add operator guide and example profiles
- test: add unit and e2e smoke tests; CI integration

Changed files (high level):
- cmd/sloctl/estimate.go (new)
- cmd/sloctl/plan.go (new)
- pkg/estimator/estimator.go (new)
- pkg/estimator/simulate.go (new)
- pkg/rollback/planner.go (new)
- examples/incidents/estimator-profile.yaml (new)
- docs/ops/rollback_planner.md (new)
- test/estimator_test.go (new)
- ci/smoke-estimator.yaml (updated)

Testing & CI: Unit tests cover estimator edge cases (zero traffic, noisy spikes), planner schema validation, and CLI flag parsing. CI runs the new smoke job (ci/smoke-estimator.yaml) which spins up the local SLO sandbox; an intermittent flake was observed initially and fixed by increasing a test timeout. Final CI status: pass.

Review summary / conversation: See review_comments for snippets. High level: reviewers asked for explicit conservatism in default profiles, clearer error messages when SLO history is sparse, and an opt-out flag for incident-bot auto-annotations. All requested changes were applied.

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-25 after approvals. No runtime changes were enabled by default; feature gated behind slo.featureEstimator and documented in ops guide.
